result.instructions:
Pinselo is a design editor (graphics, presentations, documents, websites, video). These tools create and edit the user's designs. Before designing for a brand, call get_brand_kit and use the kit whose name matches the design system or brand the user selected or named (create the design with create_design { brand_kit }). If the kit lists guidelines, read them with get_brand_guidelines first and follow them throughout: they are the brand's own rules for copy, colour, type, layout, logos and imagery. Place its logo, and use its graphics and photos with add_image { asset } wherever the design has room for a picture. Never draw an imitation of a brand element (logo, underline, brush stroke, mascot, illustration) with text or shapes when the kit has the real one, and never invent quotes, people, prices or figures. If you use an image from outside the kit or leave one out, say so in your reply. An image the user gives you (attached to the chat, or a file you can read) goes into their uploads through upload_image or create_upload_link, then into the design with add_image { asset }; never leave it out silently. When the user asks you to set up their brand in Pinselo (from a brand book, design system, website or files), make a kit with create_brand_kit, uploading its logos and images first, and change it later with update_brand_kit.
Workflow: find or create a design (list_designs, search_templates, create_design) → read it with get_design → change it with edit_design (many operations per call), whose check field lists layout problems it found (text that doesn't fit or runs off the page, poor contrast, overlaps) → fix those, then look at the result with screenshot_page. Read get_design_guide once before your first edit.
Coordinates are px at 96 dpi from the page's top-left; colours are hex. The user may have the design open: they watch your changes live, and can undo them all (undo_ai_changes, or "Undo AI changes" in the editor). Share the editUrl so they can open it.

tools.name: get_design_guide
tools.title: Design guide
tools.description: How designs, coordinates and edit operations work, plus layout and typography advice. Read once before editing.

tools.name: list_designs
tools.title: List designs
tools.description: The user's designs (own and shared), most recently edited first. Optional search text.

tools.name: list_size_presets
tools.title: Design sizes
tools.description: Size presets for create_design (Instagram post, presentation 16:9, A4, poster, video…). Optional search text.

tools.name: search_templates
tools.title: Search templates
tools.description: Find ready-made templates (and the user's team templates) to start from. Use the id with create_design.

tools.name: search_media
tools.title: Search stock media
tools.description: Free stock photos, illustrations, GIFs, stickers, video clips and music. Pass a result's provider and id to add_image as { stock: { provider, id } }, or with type video or audio to add_video or add_audio.

tools.name: list_uploads
tools.title: List uploads
tools.description: Files the user uploaded: images (photos, logos) by default, or videos and sounds with type. Use an id with add_image, add_video or add_audio as { asset: id }.

tools.name: upload_image
tools.title: Upload an image
tools.description: Put an image the user gave you into their uploads and get its asset id for add_image { asset }. file: the user's attachment, where the chat app passes attachments to tools (ChatGPT does). data_base64: a very small file, up to 64 KB, such as an SVG logo, because base64 passes through your context. For anything else, create_upload_link.

data_base64.description: The file, base64 encoded (up to 64 KB)

file.description: An image attached to the conversation, as the chat app passes it to tools

tools.name: create_upload_link
tools.title: Create an upload link
tools.description: Get a private, single-use link (15 minutes) for a file that isn't public, such as a photo for this design. If you can run commands or make HTTP requests, send the file to it yourself: curl -T <file> "<url>" (a file attached to the chat is usually at /mnt/user-data/uploads/<name>); the reply names the asset for add_image { asset }. Otherwise give the url to the user, who opens it in a browser and picks the file, and get_upload_link tells you the asset. Offer this rather than leaving an image out, and tell the user plainly if an image couldn't be included. For a brand's logos and images, upload each one and add it to a kit with create_brand_kit or update_brand_kit.

filename.description: The file's name, if you know it

purpose.description: What the file is for; shown on the page

tools.name: get_upload_link
tools.title: Check an upload link
tools.description: Whether a file has arrived through a link from create_upload_link: pending, done (with the asset ids) or expired.

tools.name: get_brand_kit
tools.title: Brand kit
tools.description: The user's brand kits (personal and team): colours, fonts for headings and body text, logos, graphics and photos (each with its asset id for add_image and file name) brand voice, and the outline of the kit's written guidelines (its brand book; read them with get_brand_guidelines). textStyles says how each kind of text looks beyond its font (weight, italic, capitals, letterSpacing, lineHeight, a reference size, allowed colours); give each text the matching role and style. missingFonts lists kit fonts that aren't uploaded yet. Check this before designing for a brand, and pass the kit's name to create_design as brand_kit.

A brand kit's written guidelines: its brand book or design system documentation (voice and copy, colour, typography, logo use, layout, imagery, motifs, dos and don'ts), in sections. Read them before designing with a kit that lists guidelines in get_brand_kit, and follow them throughout. Give the kit's name; optionally name sections to read only those (long guidelines come in parts and list the sections left).

brand_kit.description: The kit's name, as get_brand_kit lists it

sections.description: Section titles to read (matched loosely); omit for all

tools.name: get_brand_guidelines
tools.title: Brand guidelines

tools.description: Make a brand kit from a brand the user gives you (a brand book, design system, website or files): colours, fonts by role, text styles, voice, written guidelines, and logos, graphics and photos. Upload each image first with upload_image (small files such as SVG logos) or create_upload_link, and pass the asset ids it returns. The kit goes in the user's personal workspace, or in a team where they are an owner, admin or designer. Use only what the brand actually specifies; don't invent colours or rules. Returns the kit as get_brand_kit shows it, including missingFonts for fonts the user still has to upload.

fonts.description: Font family for each text role (Google Fonts from search_fonts, or the brand's own fonts, which the user uploads in Brand Hub)

graphics.description: Graphic asset ids (illustrations, patterns, icons, brush strokes)

guidelines.description: The written brand book, in sections (voice and copy, colour, typography, logo use, layout, imagery, dos and don'ts)

logos.description: Logo asset ids, from upload_image, an upload link or list_uploads

motion.description: How the brand moves (ms, px): the defaults of edit_design's animations and page transitions

stagger.description: ms between elements that appear one after another

text.description: Entrance of text (overrides enter), e.g. rise 8 px

name.description: The kit's name, usually the brand's

team.description: A team's name to make the kit in that team; omit for the personal workspace

text_styles.description: How each kind of text looks beyond its font

colors.description: Colours this text may take (any when empty)

size.description: Reference size in px for a typical page

voice.description: How the brand writes: tone, words to use and avoid

tools.name: create_brand_kit
tools.title: Create a brand kit

tools.description: Change a brand kit you can edit: give its name and only the fields to change. colors, palettes, text_styles, voice, motion, guidelines and the logos, graphics and photos lists replace what the kit has; fonts change only the roles given. To add images, upload them (upload_image or create_upload_link) and pass their asset ids in add_logos, add_graphics or add_photos; remove_assets takes images out. Returns the kit as get_brand_kit shows it.

brand_kit.description: The kit's name, as get_brand_kit lists it

colors.description: The brand's colours, named (#rrggbb) (replaces the kit's)

fonts.description: Fonts to set by role; roles left out keep their font, and "" clears one

graphics.description: Graphic asset ids (illustrations, patterns, icons, brush strokes) (replaces the kit's)

guidelines.description: The written brand book, in sections (voice and copy, colour, typography, logo use, layout, imagery, dos and don'ts) (replaces the kit's)

logos.description: Logo asset ids, from upload_image, an upload link or list_uploads (replaces the kit's)

motion.description: How the brand moves (ms, px): the defaults of edit_design's animations and page transitions

stagger.description: ms between elements that appear one after another

text.description: Entrance of text (overrides enter), e.g. rise 8 px

new_name.description: A new name for the kit

palettes.description: Named groups of colours (replaces the kit's)

remove_assets.description: Asset ids to take out of the kit's logos, graphics and photos

text_styles.description: How each kind of text looks beyond its font (replaces the kit's)

colors.description: Colours this text may take (any when empty)

size.description: Reference size in px for a typical page

voice.description: How the brand writes: tone, words to use and avoid (replaces the kit's)

tools.name: update_brand_kit
tools.title: Update a brand kit

tools.name: search_fonts
tools.title: Search fonts
tools.description: Fonts available in the editor (about 1,950 Google Fonts plus the user's brand fonts). Filter by name or category (sans, serif, display, handwriting, mono).

tools.name: create_design
tools.title: Create design
tools.description: Create a new design from a size preset, a custom size, or a template. When it's for a brand or a design system the user selected, pass that brand kit's name as brand_kit (see get_brand_kit): a team's kit puts the design in the team, and the reply and get_design then carry the kit's fonts, colours, logos, graphics and voice. Returns its id, editUrl and contents.

preset.description: Size preset id from list_size_presets, e.g. "ig-post", "presentation", "a4"

brand_kit.description: Name of the brand kit to design with (get_brand_kit), e.g. the design system the user selected

tools.name: copy_design
tools.title: Copy design
tools.description: Copy a design, optionally resized to another format (a size preset, or width and height): elements are repositioned and scaled to fit the new size. Use it to make a Story or banner version of a post, or a copy to translate. Returns the copy's id, editUrl, contents and a layout check of its pages.

preset.description: Resize to this size preset (list_size_presets), e.g. "ig-story", "presentation", "a4"

scale_content.description: Scale text and shapes with the page (default: keep their size and reposition them)

tools.name: bulk_create
tools.title: Bulk create
tools.description: Make one copy of a design per row of data (certificates, name badges, product posts, personalised invitations). In each copy, a text element bound to a column (dataBinding) gets that field's value; elsewhere each field name is replaced literally, keeping the styling, so placeholder text like "{name}" or "Jane Doe" works too. Text only; change images afterwards with edit_design. Returns the copies and a layout check of the first ones.

design_id.description: The design to copy (a template the user made, or one you prepared with placeholder text)

rows.description: One object per copy: field name (or exact placeholder text) → value

titles.description: Titles of the copies, in row order (default: the design's title and the row's first value)

tools.name: get_design
tools.title: Read design
tools.description: A design's pages and elements: ids, page-space boxes (px), text with its style, colours, images. Use the ids with edit_design.

page.description: Only this page (id or 1-based number)

tools.title: Edit design
tools.description: Apply a list of operations (add text, shapes, lines, images, videos, tables, charts, QR codes; update, delete, group, reorder; arrange, align, distribute; add, update, move and delete pages; animate elements, time them and set page lengths and transitions; add music or a voice-over and captions; replace text everywhere, keeping its style; rename). Applied in order as one change that collaborators see live. See get_design_guide.

animation.description: { in, out } entrance and exit in seconds, exactly as on update; null removes

font.description: Font family name, e.g. "Inter", "Playfair Display" (any Google Font)

# Designing in Pinselo

## Model
- A design has pages of one size (get_design → size). Every element has a page-space box x, y, w, h in px (96 dpi), measured from the page's top-left. Rotation is in degrees around the box centre.
- Elements are stacked bottom to top in the order get_design lists them; new elements go on top. Use reorder to change it.
- Types: text, shape, line, image, frame (a photo placeholder with a clip shape), group, table, chart, qr, video, embed.
- Locked elements ("locked": true) were locked by the user; you cannot move or change them.

## Editing (edit_design)
- Send all the changes for a step in one call; they apply in order as one change. Give new elements a "ref" and use "$ref" later in the same call (for example to group, arrange or align what you just added).
- Text: add_text with w (the wrap width). Leave h out so the box fits the text. Style with font, size (px), weight (100–900), color, align, lineHeight, letterSpacing, case. update with "text" replaces the words and keeps the style.
- Images: add_image takes { url } (public https), { stock: { provider, id } } from search_media, { asset } from list_uploads, upload_image or an upload link, or { brand: { kit, name } } for a file in a brand kit by its file name (the name from the design system works). fit "cover" (default) crops to fill the box.
- Files from the user: upload_image takes the attachment itself where the chat app passes attachments to tools (ChatGPT does: pass the attached file as file), or a very small file (up to 64 KB, such as an SVG logo) as data_base64, because base64 passes through your context. Otherwise create_upload_link: if you can run commands or make HTTP requests, send the file to the link yourself (curl -T <file> "<url>"; a file attached to the chat is usually at /mnt/user-data/uploads/<name>) and the reply names the asset. If you can't, give the user the link: they drop the file on that page, and get_upload_link tells you the asset. Offer this rather than leaving an image out, and if an image still couldn't be included, say so plainly.
- Layout: arrange stacks items in a row or column or on a grid, with gap, align, justify and stretch; within "page" lays them out inside the page minus padding. align and distribute line items up with the page or with each other.
- Pages: add_page (optionally duplicate an existing page), update_page (background, title, speaker notes, duration, transition), move_page, delete_page.
- Text everywhere: replace_text swaps every match of find for replace across the design (or one page, or given elements) and keeps each word's styling. Use it to fill in a template's placeholder text, rename a product, or translate (one replace_text per sentence).
- Other formats: copy_design makes a copy, optionally resized to another preset (an Instagram story from a post, a banner, A4). Elements are repositioned to fit; fix what its check reports. Copy first when translating, so the original stays.
- Many versions from data: bulk_create makes one copy per row (certificates, badges, a post per product). Put placeholder text in the design first (for example "{name}"), then pass rows like { "{name}": "Ada" }; elements bound to a column take the value for that column name. Its warning lists fields that matched nothing.
- Shapes: rect, ellipse, triangle, right-triangle, diamond, squircle, pill, half-circle, arch, ring, block-arc, pie, snip-corner, snip-two, round-one, plaque, folded-corner, frame, ticket, cylinder, cube, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, polygon, parallelogram, trapezoid, shield, star, star-6, star-8, starburst-12, burst, seal, badge, sparkle, sun, gear, flower, heart, moon, drop, leaf, cloud, lightning, blob, cross, plus, cross-x, check, arrow, double-arrow, chevron, chevron-double, curved-arrow, u-turn-arrow, circular-arrow, tag, ribbon, flag, banner, wave, speech, callout-rect, callout-round, thought-bubble, document, multi-document, predefined-process, manual-input, delay, off-page, internal-storage, display.
- Charts: column, bar, stacked-column, stacked-bar, line, area, combo, pie, donut, scatter, bubble, radar, funnel, progress-ring, progress-bar, gauge.

## Video and motion
- Sizes for social video: create_design { preset } with fb-reel or ig-reel (1080×1920, Reels and Stories), ig-video (1080×1350, feed) or video-square (1080×1080). These open as videos in the editor.
- Times are in seconds. Pages play one after another in videos, GIFs and auto-playing presentations: update_page { duration, transition: { type, duration } } sets a page's length (null: automatic, 5 s or its videos' length) and how it comes in from the page before (fade, slide, push, wipe, zoom, …; none cuts). An ad usually needs scenes of 1.5–3 s with short transitions (0.2–0.4 s). get_design's timeline lists page lengths, the soundtrack and captions.
- Elements: animation { in: { type, delay, duration, easing, distance }, out: { type, at, duration } } on any add_* or update. in.type: fade, rise, drop, slide-left/-right/-up/-down, scale, zoom, pop, wipe, draw (a line draws itself from its first point to its last), typewriter (text), blur; text can also animate by line, word or letter (by, stagger). delay counts from when the element appears; out.at is the page second the exit starts. visibleFrom / visibleTo show an element for part of a page, so one page can swap texts. animation null removes both.
- Staggering: animate { ids, in, start, stagger } gives the listed elements the same entrance one after another (for example eyebrow, then headline, then button).
- Brand motion: a kit with motion (get_brand_kit, get_design) sets the defaults: what an animation leaves out (type, duration, easing, distance; text and drawn lines separately), the stagger, the page transition, and bounce: false rules out pop. Leave those values out so the brand's own style applies; set motion on the kit with update_brand_kit when the user's brand book describes how it moves.
- Sound and video: add_audio adds music or a voice-over (an upload via list_uploads { type: "audio" }, search_media { type: "audio" }, or a URL); by default it runs to the end of the video and loops if shorter, with volume, fadeIn and fadeOut. Set page lengths first, or run update_audio { id, fit: true } after changing them. add_video places a clip (trim, muted, loop, fit, volume); a page lasts as long as its videos unless its duration is set.
- Captions: most people watch social video without sound, so put the message on screen and caption any voice-over with set_captions { cues: [{ start, end, text }] } (video seconds).
- Check motion: screenshot_page { time } shows a page at one second, { frames: 6 } a filmstrip across it. edit_design's check reports text on screen too briefly to read (about 3 words a second plus half a second), text and buttons in the part of a 9:16 video that Reels and Stories cover (keep them between 14% and 65% of the height), and a video too long for its format.
- Export: export_design { format: "mp4", pages } plays the pages given at the design's own size (scale or width to change it).

## Good design
- Start from the brand kit (get_brand_kit) whose name matches the design system or brand the user selected or named, and use only that kit's assets; if several could match, ask. Create the design with create_design { brand_kit } so it is made where the kit's fonts live and get_design keeps showing the kit. Its voice sums up how the brand writes: follow it for every word. A kit that lists guidelines has a full written brand book: read it with get_brand_guidelines before you design, and let it win over the general advice here. If the kit lists missingFonts, still use those fonts for their roles and tell the user to upload them. Use its colours, its fonts for each role, its textStyles (set every text's role, and its weight, italic, case, letterSpacing, lineHeight and colour as the matching style says; size is a reference for a typical page, scale it to the format; edit_design's check and get_design's styleCheck list text that strays), its logo, and its graphics and photos: each comes with an asset id and file name, so choose by name and check with screenshot_page (a logo that suits the background, for example). A design system in the chat gives you colours, fonts and rules, but its files can't reach Pinselo from there, so use the kit's copies; if there is no kit for it yet and the user wants one, make it with create_brand_kit (upload the logos and images first with upload_image or create_upload_link and pass their asset ids). Prefer a real image to a type-only layout when the format has room. Never draw an imitation of a brand element (logo, underline, brush stroke, mascot, illustration) with text or shapes when the kit has the real one: look through its graphics first. Use only facts the user or the brand gave you: never invent quotes, people, prices or figures, and mark anything you must assume as a placeholder and say so. If the kit lacks something the design needs, finish with what's there and say exactly what's missing. When a team's kit governs the design, get_design shows it as brand (fonts by role, colours); if brand.enforced is set, edit_design only accepts those colours and fonts.
- Give elements a role (headline, subhead, body, cta, logo, hero-image, price, legal, …) when you add them, and use the brand font for that role. Roles keep the hierarchy clear for later edits and resizes.
- Prefer a template (search_templates → create_design with template_id) for common formats; then replace its text (replace_text) and images.
- Give each page one clear focal point. Use size and weight for hierarchy (for example a 1080 px square post: headline 72–110 px, body 28–36 px).
- Keep margins generous (about 5–8% of the page width) and keep spacing consistent; align edges to each other.
- Use at most two font families. Keep strong contrast between text and its background (dark on light or light on dark; check with a screenshot).
- Presentations: one idea per slide, short text, large visuals; put the full script in speaker notes.
- Fix every problem edit_design reports in its check field, then judge the overall look with screenshot_page.
